predecessors.name: Second French Empire
predecessors.text: France as the Second Empire left it on 4 September 1870, Alsace-Lorraine included

successors.name: Vichy France
successors.text: the part of France not occupied in 1940, under Petain: 'Vichy France declared: 10 July 1940'

successors.name: Nazi Germany
successors.text: the north and the Atlantic coast, occupied by Germany after the Battle of France (10 May - 25 June 1940); the page gives 'Nazi forces occupied much of France' without zone boundaries

ledger.x: 4 September 1870: the Third Republic is proclaimed in Paris.
September 1870: the republic continues the war.
December 1870: the Confederation becomes the German Empire.
1871: the government moves to Versailles.
January 1871: the war goes on against the German Empire.
28 January 1871: the armistice.
1871: German troops stay on French soil as a guarantee.
Late March 1871: the Paris Commune seizes Paris.
May 1871: the government suppresses the Commune ('suppressed by the government in May'); the page gives 'late March through May 1871'.
10 May 1871: France cedes Alsace-Lorraine.
September 1873: the last German troops leave French soil.
1885: a protectorate over northern and central Vietnam.
Late 1914: Germany occupies the north-east.
5 October 1915: the Army of the Orient lands at Salonika.
February-April 1917: the Germans fall back to the Hindenburg Line.
Spring 1918: the German offensive retakes ground.
30 September 1918: the Macedonian front ends.
8 October 1918: French troops land at Beirut.
17 November 1918: French troops land in Cilicia.
11 November 1918: the armistice.
1 December 1918: the Allies occupy the Rhineland.
28 June 1919: Alsace-Lorraine returns to France.
January 1920: the French fight the Turkish national forces in Cilicia.
25 April 1920: France receives the mandate for Syria and Lebanon.
ledger.cpn: French Mandate for Syria and the Lebanon

ledger.x: April 1920: the coast of Lebanon passes from military occupation to the mandate (25 April 1920, the grant; Greater Lebanon proclaimed 1 September 1920).
20 October 1921: the Treaty of Ankara.
3-7 January 1922: the French leave Cilicia.
11 January 1923: France and Belgium occupy the Ruhr.
25 August 1925: the Ruhr is evacuated.
30 June 1930: the Rhineland occupation ends.
June 1940: Germany occupies the north and west.
10 July 1940: the Republic ends; the occupation continues under the successors (nazi-germany and vichy-france dossiers).

10 July 1940: the Republic's mandate over Syria and Lebanon passes to Vichy France; the mandate itself ran until 1946 (Mandate page: 'The French mandate lasted until 1946, when French troops finally left Syria and Lebanon').
ledger.cpn: French Mandate for Syria and the Lebanon

ledger.x: 10 July 1940: the Indochinese protectorates pass to Vichy France (the dossier ends here; the protectorate itself continues under Vichy France, which the french-indochina dossier carries).
10 July 1940: the Third Republic ends.

wars.name: Franco-Prussian War
wars.outcome: German victory: war from 19 July 1870 to 28 January 1871; France ceded most of Alsace and parts of Lorraine ('as well as most of Alsace and parts of Lorraine'), paid 5 billion francs in gold and endured a German occupation of parts of France until September…

wars.name: Paris Commune
wars.outcome: The Commune held Paris 'from late March through May 1871' and was suppressed by the government in May.

wars.name: World War I (Western Front)
wars.outcome: Trench warfare from the Swiss frontier to the North Sea; Germany held 64 percent of French pig-iron production in the occupied zone; Operation Alberich (25 February-5 April 1917) and the Armistice of 11 November 1918 returned the ground.

wars.name: Macedonian front
wars.outcome: Armistice of Salonica on 29 September 1918; the front ended at noon on 30 September 1918.

wars.name: Franco-Turkish War
wars.outcome: Treaty of Ankara, 20 October 1921; the French left Cilicia on 3-7 January 1922; the sanjak of Alexandretta stayed under French control.

wars.name: Franco-Syrian War
wars.outcome: General Gouraud's ultimatum to Faisal on 14 July 1920; the French won at Maysaloun in less than a day and General Goybet 'captured Damascus with little resistance' on 24 July 1920.

wars.name: Occupation of the Ruhr
wars.outcome: France and Belgium occupied the Ruhr from 11 January 1923; evacuation completed 25 August 1925 after the Dawes Plan.

wars.name: Battle of France
wars.outcome: 10 May - 25 June 1940; the Republic ended on 10 July 1940 and Vichy France was declared.

certainty.note: The metropolitan frontier is a treaty line, sharp from the Treaty of Frankfurt (10 May 1871); the 1870-1873 occupation zone is soft and the Guiana frontiers with Suriname and Brazil are the least sure part of the shape.
The front line moved every month; the metropolitan frontier is unchanged but the held ground (occupation and contest) is soft.
Treaty of Versailles frontier from 28 June 1919; the Rhineland, Ruhr and Cilicia occupation zones are soft, and the 1940 occupation zone has no boundary on the page.
